title: Zhen Im
text:
Welcome!
I am an Associate Professor in the Department of Social Sciences at Lappeenranta-Lahti University of Technology (LUT). I am also an Academy Research Fellow funded by the Research Council of Finland (2026–2030). Previously, I held postdoctoral research positions at LUT University and Copenhagen Business School. I received my PhD in Social Sciences from the University of Helsinki.
My research focuses broadly on the relationship between work and politics. In particular, I examine how transformations in work driven by technological change and the green transition shape political attitudes and behaviour, with an emphasis on perceptions of social standing and fairness.

title: Zhen Im
text:
Current research projects
My current research project, GREENSHUFFLE, examines whether and how the green transition shapes citizens’ perceptions of the social standing of different occupations, the extent to which these changes are contested, and the political consequences of such contestation. The project runs from 2026 to 2030 and is funded by the Research Council of Finland through an Academy Research Fellowship.
I also lead a work package in the Just-In-Clime research consortium. The work package examines how experts and citizens discuss justice in the context of the just transition across high-, middle-, and low-income countries. The consortium runs from 2026 to 2030 and is funded by Horizon Europe under HORIZON-CL5-2025-06.

title: Research
text: My work examines how large-scale economic transformations become personally experienced and politically consequential. It focuses on three connected areas.

title: Research
section: Regional knowledge economies and subjective mobility
text:
Regional knowledge economies and subjective mobility
This research investigates how geographically uneven knowledge-intensive growth relates to people’s perceptions of social mobility and to regional political outcomes.

title: Research
text:
Occupational recognition and social valuation
This strand examines how occupations acquire status and social value, and how workers respond when they expect their work to become less valued.

title: Research
text:
Work and the green transition
This comparative project studies perceived job risk and anticipated societal devaluation associated with decarbonisation across advanced economies. It distinguishes material insecurity from concerns about recognition and social worth.

title: Research
text:
Methods
I use comparative survey research, multilevel models, regional panel analysis, occupational data, and quantitative text analysis.
